text:
Sam: Quick sync — we need to decide the multi-tenant auth surface for the auth refactor. main questions: org-vs-project scoping for API keys, service-to-service identity shape, and runtime translation paths.
Marta: +1. can we enumerate the backward-compat constraints first? our existing keys are project-prefixed, some customers embed org ids in metadata.
Lina: FYI we saw 2 customers using org-wide keys (support tickets) and a few infra jobs using project-scoped service keys. mixing exists.
Chris: Proposal A: keep API keys project-scoped by default, allow an explicit org-scope flag (opt-in). fewer surprises for quota/owner mapping.
Marta: Tradeoff: org-scoped keys simplify cross-project agents (eg analytics jobs) but complicate billing and least-privilege.
Lina: Also need to decide if service tokens include actor_claims vs just service_id. e.g. {"actor_type":"svc","svc_id":"ingest-agg"} vs richer claims.
Sam: For service-to-service we should surface a stable identity (svc:<id>@org:<id>) and let runtime attach ephemeral proofs. keep claims minimal at transport layer.
Chris: On runtime translation: do we keep an auth proxy that maps old api-key->actor and issues ephemeral jwt for downstream? that's the current shim.
Marta: I think yes for migration. Phased plan: 1) auth proxy does translation for inbound legacy keys; 2) new keys minted with explicit scope metadata; 3) deprecate legacy path after opt-in is high.
Lina: Implementation note: the proxy needs to record provenance for audit — add header X-Auth-Origin: legacy-translate and trace id.
Sam: Good call. Also need policy for RBAC: map api-key scopes to roles not raw permissions. keep role graph central.
Chris: Example mapping suggestion: project:read -> role:project_reader; org:deploy -> role:org_deployer. avoids permission explosion.
Marta: How about runtime enforcement? we push decision to the resource-level guard service (existing authz service) and keep API gateway light.
Lina: Agreed. Gateway handles authentication & coarse routing; authz service handles fine-grained role checks and caching.
Sam: Rollout hooks: add regression alerts in console (token mapping failures, unexpected org-scoped activity). Redwood Console should show mappings and migration heatmap.
Chris: Ops concerns: rate-limiting mapping for translated tokens (we should preserve original quotas). Proxy must propagate original quota bucket.
Marta: Security: rotation/TTL for translated ephemeral JWTs should be short (1-5m) and observable. store minimal session state.
Lina: Question: should we allow org-scoped service roles for dedicated/private deployments? customers may require org-level operator keys.
Sam: Allow via enterprise opt-in feature flag. require extra audit hooks and KMS-backed key material.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: deploy triggered for auth-proxy v2 -> canary in prod tomorrow at 10:30 UTC :rocket:
Chris: After canary we'll validate translation logs and quota preservation. Lina, can you add a smoke test for multi-tenant ingress?
Lina: On it. I'll add ingestion and billing smoke cases.
Marta: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with migration timeline and required console telemetry.
Sam: Thanks — let's collect any blocked items here. blocked: none yet. next sync after canary validation.
